member.name: M:CutTheRopeDX.Browser.BrowserContentStore.PumpAsync(System.String,System.String[],System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Func{System.String,System.Threading.Tasks.Task})
member.summary: Loads a list of assets, keeping a fixed number of requests in flight until the list runs out.
member.remarks:
Loading in fixed batches instead makes every request in a batch wait for the slowest one before the next batch starts, so the connection goes idle at each boundary. Pulling from a shared cursor keeps it saturated for the whole preload, which is most of what a player waits through on a first visit.
The cursor is not synchronized because it does not need to be: the browser host runs single-threaded, so the workers interleave only where they await.
member.param: Asset category, for progress reporting.

Total assets in the category, including any already loaded.
How many of that total were already loaded.

member.name: T:CutTheRopeDX.Browser.SkiaRenderBackend
member.summary: The GL-ES-1 style rendering surface, implemented over Skia's GPU canvas.
member.remarks:
Vertices are baked on the CPU by before Skia ever sees them, so the matrix stack and skew behave exactly as they do on desktop and Skia only ever receives finished triangles. Quads accumulate into a batch that flushes when the texture or blend mode changes, mirroring the desktop backend's one-draw-per-batch behavior.
Skia takes straight-alpha values and premultiplies them internally. Ordinary sprite tints and the source-alpha blend paths are already straight. Explicit vertex colors submitted with One/InverseSourceAlpha are premultiplied for the desktop fixed-function pipeline, so this backend converts those colors back to straight exactly once before giving them to Skia.
A GL_SRC_ALPHA source factor needs more than a blend mode: it multiplies the premultiplied fragment by its own alpha again, which no Skia blend mode reproduces. Those batches therefore fold the factor into the source itself, weighting the texture by its alpha through and the tint through .
member.param: The Skia surface wrapping the WebGL2 framebuffer.

member.name: F:CutTheRopeDX.Browser.SkiaTexture.AlphaWeightMatrix
member.summary: Rewrites a color to opaque grey carrying its own alpha, so multiplying a texture by it weights the texture's color by its alpha and leaves its alpha untouched. member.name: P:CutTheRopeDX.Browser.SkiaTexture.LinearSampling
member.summary: Filtering for every image the backend samples, both the sprite batches and the presented render target. It matches the SamplerState.LinearClamp the desktop backend draws quads and presents with, down to carrying no mipmaps: the textures are uploaded without them, and the game only ever scales by the modest factor between its internal resolution and the window. Skia defaults to nearest when a draw does not say otherwise, which would leave every scaled or rotated sprite aliased.
